cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to talk about another sorting algorithm which is merge sort.
Merge sort algorithm is divide and conquer algorithm.
So in case of divide and conquer algorithm we divide the big problem into small chunks.
And when the chunk becomes extremely small such that we cannot divide it further, then we start merge
them and we are able to get the final answer.
So we are going to look at the unsorted array to see how the merge sort works.
So I'm just going to put this array like this to have a more space over here.
Now the first thing that we will do we are going to divide this array into two halves.
Then it will be divided into two halves again each array.
And we continue this until we have one single element in each array.
So when we have a single element in the array, it means that by definition it is sorted because we
have only one element.
So what we can do as a next step is we are going to take these two elements and combine together in
a one array in a sorted way, and we will do the same thing for the next two elements and combine them
together in a sorted way.
And we will do the same thing for the next two elements, and we are going to combine them in a sorted
way.
And for these two also, we are going to combine them in a sorted way.
Then we will take these two arrays and combine them together one more time in a sorted way.
So it's going to be like this.
Then we are going to take these two arrays and combine them together in a sorted way, and it's going
to be like this.
Then at the end, we are just going to take these two arrays and combine in a main array in a sorted
way.
So that's how the logic behind the merge sort algorithm works.
Now when you first look at this, you might think that this is really inefficient to break down all
of the elements into single arrays.
But it's not like that.
It's actually incredibly efficient sorting algorithm.
Now in case of merge sort algorithm we are going to use the helper method.
